title: aggeodata: multi-source climate and soil data ingestion and datacube builder for agricultural research
description:
aggeodata is a Python package for downloading daily gridded climate data and soil data, and assembling them into analysis-ready NetCDF datacubes aligned to a common grid and CRS. It supports agricultural and climate change research in the CGIAR Climate Data Hub (CDH).

Supported sources:

  • CHIRPS: precipitation (0.05°, 1981–present).
  • CHIRTS: maximum and minimum temperature (0.05°, 1983–present).
  • AgERA5: solar radiation, wind, relative humidity, vapour pressure deficit and other agrometeorological variables (0.1°, 1979–present).
  • NASA POWER: solar radiation, wind and temperature (0.5°, 1981–present).
  • SoilGrids v2: 12 soil properties at 1 km (default) or 250 m (ISRIC).

Besides the official endpoints, aggeodata can read cloud-optimized Zarr v3 datacubes: the CDH mirrors of CHIRPS v3 daily, CHIRTS-ERA5 daily and SoilGrids v2 (1 km) on Hugging Face, and the ECMWF ARCO store for AgERA5. With these stores, a bounding box and date range is a single indexed read instead of many per-day downloads. All backends write the same per-day NetCDF layout, so the datacube step does not change.

The package also includes an MCP server for use with AI agents and is used by the CDH AI agent skills. Documentation: https://github.com/CGIAR-Climate-Data-Hub/aggeodata.
